items.case: PIL on homeless and demolition-displaced voters, Delhi High Court
items.headline: Delhi SIR: plea to include homeless and demolition-displaced voters
items.claim: A PIL asked the Delhi High Court for special arrangements so homeless and displaced people could enrol in the revision, and the Court reserved its order and said it would not monitor the policy, LiveLaw reported. LiveLaw reported on 1 September that the bench of Chief Justice D.K. Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia had dismissed the petition. The Court said the Commission's Manual on Electoral Rolls already provides, in clause 8.5, how a homeless person's ordinary residence is determined, so the fear that homeless people would be left off the draft appeared to be without basis. It said any elector left off the roll after a demolition or relocation can file Form 6.
items.quote: everything cannot be thrust upon courts
items.response: The Court said the petition gave no particulars or numbers of people displaced by demolitions who remained off the roll. The Commission told the Court that clause 8.5 lets homeless people enrol without documentary proof of residence once a booth level officer has verified over more than one night that they are present at the address given, Bar and Bench reported.
items.note: Dismissal: LiveLaw, by Malavika Prasad, published 1 September 2026, 4:05 pm IST, 2026 LiveLaw (Del) 797, W.P.(C) 11942/2026, https://www.livelaw.in/high-court/delhi-high-court/delhi-high-court-rejects-pil-include-homeless-demolition-displaced-persons-sir-548104 ; Bar and Bench, by Prashant Jha, published 1 September 2026, 9:57 am IST. items.case: Writ Petition No. 732 of 2026, a family's petition on deletion after Form 8, Bombay High Court at Goa
items.headline: 'No Business Asking Them to Fill Form 6 Because System Didn't Allow Form 8': Bombay HC Condemns ECI's Handling of SIR Process
items.claim: A family of six who moved house within the same constituency filed Form 8 and were then deleted from the roll, because the ERONET software found no record of their cards and allowed only a rejection. The bench asked the Commission to show where the law allows a deletion without a hearing and said the family should not have been asked to file Form 6, The Wire reported, citing The Times of India.
items.quote: Questioning the legality of the removal of the Santa Cruz family from the voter list without a hearing, the bench noted, "Show us from the Act where it empowers you to delete without hearing. If you are planning to remove someone's name, you have to give the person an opportunity of hearing first." ... According to TOI, the bench replied, "You have no business asking them to fill Form 6 because the system didn't allow you to do it on Form 8. That was the problem."
items.response: The Wire reported that the Commission's counsel said other voters deleted in the same way had been put back on the roll after filing Form 6, and that the family had not filed Form 6 when asked to.
items.note: PTI via Telangana Today (1 Oct 2026, 11:18 AM) agrees on the hearing date (Wednesday 30 Sept), the bench, the six family members in Santa Cruz, Form 8, ERONET offering only 'reject', and the bench's 'Show us from the Act...what empowers you to delete without hearing?'. It adds that the court said the draft roll cannot be the basis for deletion. It does not carry the 'no business' line, which The Wire attributes to TOI. Both sources name the petitioner; the draft does not.

items.case: Writ Petition No. 732 of 2026, a family's petition on deletion after Form 8, Bombay High Court at Goa
items.headline: 'What Is SIR's Purpose If Citizens Are Being Removed From Voter's List? Bombay High Court Asks ECI
items.claim: At a further hearing of the same family's petition the bench asked what purpose the revision served if citizens were left off the roll. It also asked why a voter who had moved house should have to sign the enumeration form, whose declaration says the voter still lives at the address on the existing roll, LiveLaw reported.
items.quote: "Read the judgment, it says ECI has an obligation to ensure that all Indian citizens are on the list... If citizens are excluded what will we do with your SIR? If citizens are being removed from the list then what is the purpose of this entire SIR process then?" ... "If a voter comes to you with Form 8, saying he has changed his address you just cannot tell that person that look your name isn't included in the draft roll now you will have to fill in Form 6 (inclusion of new voter). Your enumeration form, basically has a declaration that a person continues to live in the address as mentioned in the existing voters list. But consider, if someone has changed their residence, can you compel the person to make a false declaration by submitting that pre-filled enumeration? Why can't that person simply give a Form 8 because anyway, his name is there in the existing list he just wants to get his address changed.. Why compel enumeration form?" Justice Menezes observed.
items.response: LiveLaw reported that the Commission's counsel argued that a voter had to submit the enumeration form along with Form 8 to have an address changed, and that a voter who did not submit it had to file Form 6.

items.case: Petition on the implementation of the SIR in Maharashtra, Bombay High Court
items.headline: Maharashtra SIR: Bombay High Court Declines Oral Plea To Restrain ECI From Deleting Voters' Names, Says SC Seized Of Issue
items.claim: The Chief Justice's bench refused an oral request to order that no names be deleted from the roll in Maharashtra for the time being. It said it would follow the Supreme Court, which it was told had restrained High Courts in November 2025 from hearing petitions on the revision, and adjourned the case by four weeks, LiveLaw reported. The petition asks for the order and reasons behind the revision in the state and for safeguards against wrongful exclusion.
items.quote: "There are restraining orders already... No purpose will be served by a parallel litigation. Let the SC hear the matter first and we will consider it later," Chief Justice said. ... The judges turned down the said oral prayer, by observing, "No no no...we are not going to pass any such orders... We will follow judicial propriety." The bench accordingly, adjourned the hearing for four weeks.
items.note: LiveLaw gives no case number. The petition alleges BLOs in Maharashtra asked for supporting documents with enumeration forms; that is the petitioners' allegation and is left out of the claim.

items.case: MA Baby v. Union of India and others, WP(c) 63560/2026, Supreme Court
items.headline: Don't Completely Stop Trains/Metro In Delhi To Handle October 10 Protests : Supreme Court To Centre
items.claim: The Supreme Court told the Centre not to stop all trains and Metro services in Delhi before the 10 October protests against the Chief Election Commissioner, and to run them in a regulated way, LiveLaw reported. The petition was brought by CPI(M) General Secretary MA Baby and others against the closure of 57 Metro stations and the cancellation of trains due at New Delhi and Nizamuddin. The order said the notifications appeared to be overreaching, and ETV Bharat reported that the bench also asked the Centre to reconsider Jantar Mantar as the designated protest site.
items.quote: there shall be no outright prohibition on the movement of Metro trains
items.response: The order records that the Solicitor General "has fairly agreed to impress upon the authorities to reassess such prohibitions." He said the impression that the whole city had been shut "is far from the truth."
items.note: One item for two reports of the same order: LiveLaw (553920, with the case number) and ETV Bharat. ETV Bharat prints the order's sentence as "We make it clear that there shall not be complete prohibition on movement of Metro/trains"; LiveLaw's wording is used here. The 57 stations are the Court's figure and the train times Kapil Sibal's statement, per LiveLaw 553880. The protest was called by the Cockroach Janta Party and opposition parties.

items.case: Contempt petition against the Union Home Secretary, the Delhi Police Commissioner and the DMRC chairperson, Supreme Court
items.headline: Supreme Court Contempt Plea Alleges Delhi Authorities Defied Order On Metro, Train Curbs
items.claim: A contempt plea filed in the Supreme Court on 10 October alleged that the Centre and Delhi authorities defied the Court's order of 9 October, keeping 57 Metro stations shut and cancelling Delhi-bound trains before the protest against the Chief Election Commissioner, Outlook reported. The plea also said no traffic advisory had been published in newspapers. A bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana listed it to be heard with a petition against the detention of opposition leaders at a special sitting on Sunday 11 October, Bar and Bench reported. On 15 October, before the Chief Justice and Justice Bagchi, the Delhi Police Commissioner filed two affidavits that tendered an unconditional apology for any perceived non-compliance and said there had been no non-compliance with the Court's orders of 9 and 11 October. Justice Bagchi observed that on the Solicitor General's account the apology appeared qualified.
items.quote: "Notwithstanding the solemn judicial mandate and the assurance recorded before the bench of the Chief Justice of India (CJI), the contemnors have consciously maintained a blanket shutdown across transit corridors, persisted with unwarranted train cancellations, and failed to issue or publicize transparent traffic and transit advisories."
items.response: The Solicitor General said the apology was included as standard practice in answering a contempt notice and that the government was defending its actions on facts. The Commissioner asked for the contempt notice to be discharged.
items.note: Outlook and Hindustan Times name different advocates as the filer; the filer is left out. The plea is the petitioner's allegation. The special sitting is from Bar and Bench, by Debayan Roy, 10 October 2026, 8:09 pm IST (https://www.barandbench.com/news/delhi-protests-supreme-court-to-hold-special-sunday-sitting-to-hear-pleas-against-detention-of-opposition-leaders), which also names the filer and the three officials; the filer stays out. The affidavits and the exchange of 15 October are from Bar and Bench, by Ritwik Choudhury, 15 October 2026, 6:30 pm IST (modified 17 October). The quoted words of the affidavits are 'unconditional and unqualified apology' and 'no non-compliance much less any wilful or deliberate non-compliance'.

items.case: Application by five deleted electors in the West Bengal SIR matter, Supreme Court
items.headline: 'We Are Conscious' : Supreme Court To Consider Plea To Prioritise SIR-Deleted Voters' Appeals Ahead Of Kolkata, Howrah Municipal Elections
items.claim: Counsel for electors deleted from West Bengal's roll after adjudication asked the Supreme Court to hear their plea before the Kolkata and Howrah municipal elections and to let appellants vote, LiveLaw reported. The Chief Justice said the Court would try to list it on 16 October, or else on 29 October, and suggested the tribunals take up appeals for inclusion first and appeals seeking deletion last. Counsel told the Court that nearly 1.70 lakh appeals from the two municipal areas were pending.
items.quote: We will find out if we can list on 16th (Friday) ...otherwise 29th is best way.
items.response: No submission by the Commission was reported. The figures put to the Court were counsel's, partly drawn from the Commission's affidavits.
items.note: Mentioned on Friday 9 October before CJI Surya Kant, Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana. UNI confirms the 16 October listing. Counsel said the main West Bengal SIR matter had been put back to 30 October.

items.case: Paka Suresh v. Union of India, SLP(C) No. 35786/2026, Supreme Court
items.headline: Andhra Pradesh Local Body Elections | Conduct Polls As Per Old Rolls If SIR Not Complete Before Notification: Supreme Court
items.claim: The Supreme Court, hearing a challenge to the Andhra Pradesh High Court's order for local body elections within six weeks, said the elections should use the revised roll if it is published before the polls are notified, and the existing roll if it is not. It said the roll in force applies until the Commission publishes the revised list and that the revision cannot be a reason to delay the polls.
items.quote: However, if the final SIR rolls were not published before the notification, the elections would be conducted using the existing electoral rolls in accordance with the applicable State laws.
items.response: The bench noted that the Election Commission had proposed to publish the final roll on 16 October 2026. Senior counsel for the State Election Commission said the rolls in force continue until the Commission publishes a fresh list. Deccan Chronicle reported on 15 October that the Commission had moved the final publication in Andhra Pradesh to 30 October and the last date for disposing of claims and objections to 22 October. The Wire reported that the YSRCP moved the Supreme Court on 20 October, alleging that violence during the filing of nominations for the state's urban local body elections kept its candidates from taking part.
items.note: Bench of CJI Surya Kant, Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, Friday 9 October. The petitioner's counsel's figure of about 44 lakh voters removed is a party's submission and is left out. items.case: WP 32975 of 2026, a petition by two electors, Telangana High Court
items.headline: Telangana SIR | Plea Challenges 'AI-Based' SIR Process; High Court Asks ECI Why Voter Was Excluded Without Notice
items.claim: The Telangana High Court asked the Commission why one petitioner was left off the roll without a notice and what happened to the other after his hearing, LiveLaw reported. The petition challenges notices over minor discrepancies and the automated matching used in the revision. The case was listed again for 13 October. items.case: Rahul Gandhi v. Election Commission of India, W.P.(C) No. 1351 of 2026 (Diary No. 64196 of 2026), Supreme Court
items.headline: SC registry points out 10 defects in Rahul Gandhi's plea in SIR case
items.claim: Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge and other INDIA bloc leaders filed a writ petition in the Supreme Court on 12 October against the Election Commission, the Chief Election Commissioner and the two Election Commissioners. Delhi Police had stopped their march to the Court on Bhagwant Das Road earlier that day, and counsel filed the petition shortly before the filing counter closed. The petition asks for the SIR to be suspended in every state while the case is heard, for a committee under a retired Supreme Court judge to audit the names left off or deleted, and for the Commission's files on its decision to hold the revision. PTI reported that the Registry flagged more than ten defects in it, among them illegible or missing pages, an unclear copy of Kharge's identity card and a court fee short by over Rs 200. LawBeat reported that the Registry registered it on 13 October once the defects were cured.

items.case: W.P.(C) 14955/2026, a petition by two electors, Delhi High Court
items.headline: Delhi High Court closes a petition by two electors left off the roll and leaves them free to file Form 6
items.claim: The Delhi High Court closed a petition by two electors whose names were left off Delhi's roll after they moved house and could not fill the enumeration form. They had asked the Court to quash para 4(c) of the SIR guidelines, which sends such electors to Form 6 with the declaration, and to restore their entries and let them correct them through Form 8. The Commission's standing counsel said they could file Form 6 and that the Electoral Registration Officer would help. The first petitioner said that filing Form 6 would be a false declaration. The bench said that, since the suggestion came from the Commission's counsel on the officer's instructions, his fear of being accused of a false declaration was misplaced. It left them free to file Form 6, to be processed in accordance with law.
items.quote: Having heard learned counsel for the parties, we are of the considered opinion that when the suggestion is coming from the learned standing counsel appearing for ECI, that too as per the instructions of the Electoral Registration Officer, petitioner no.1’s apprehension that he would be accused of furnishing a false declaration is misplaced. ... With these observations, the writ proceedings are closed. Petitioners, if so desire, may fill Form 6, which shall be processed in accordance with law.
items.response: The Commission's standing counsel said the grievance could be redressed if the petitioners filed Form 6 under rule 25(2) read with rule 13(1)(a) of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, and that he had asked the first petitioner to do so at the previous hearing and the Electoral Registration Officer would help.

items.case: Appeals by the Election Commission before West Bengal's SIR appellate tribunals
items.headline: Election Commission Seeks to Remove Half the Bengal Voters Judges Have Cleared For Inclusion
items.claim: The Election Commission had filed appeals before West Bengal's SIR appellate tribunals against the inclusion of at least 14,75,887 voters by 17 October, 49.2% of the 30,00,545 voters in the records whom judicial officers had examined and found eligible, The Wire reported from appeal records collected by the Civic Research Group. Malda, Murshidabad and Uttar Dinajpur hold 44.6% of these appeals. In the 41 seats where minorities are more than half the population the appeals equal 5.9% of the draft roll, and in the 89 seats where they are under 10% they equal 0.6%. The tribunals had decided 80,091 appeals, or 5.4%, and the report says no tribunal has been able to upload an order since 21 September. In a follow-up on 24 October, The Wire reported that the Civic Research Group's fuller records show 16,08,175 appeals by the Commission against 32,53,401 voters found eligible, 49.4%, close to the 16,10,311 appeals against inclusion that the Commission reported to the Supreme Court in September. It reported that the appeal numbers carry a filing date, a structure that activists found and The Wire says it verified, and that 13,85,374 of the 13,95,794 appeal IDs in an earlier extract of 17 October, or 99.3%, carry one of three dates, 5, 6 or 8 April 2026, with more than 12 lakh on 5 April. The roll was frozen for the Assembly election at midnight on 7 April.
items.quote: The Commission has not disclosed on what grounds it is challenging these voters, and who exactly decided to file the appeals.
items.response: The report says the Commission has not said on what grounds it filed the appeals, who decided to file them, or whether each case was reviewed before an appeal was filed. The follow-up says only the Commission can confirm the dates read from the appeal numbers, and that a single date on more than 12 lakh appeals does not by itself show who authorised them.
items.note: The Wire, went live 21 October 2026, 7:23 pm (article:published_date 2026-10-21T13:53:24+05:30), read in full on 22 October 2026 via Firecrawl and again through The Wire's CMS API on 24 October 2026, which gives the byline as Aparna Bhattacharya. items.case: W.P.(C) No. 1330 of 2026, a petition on voter deletions in Maharashtra's SIR, Supreme Court
items.headline: Supreme Court assures no deleted voters will be prosecuted for submitting Form 6
items.claim: The Supreme Court issued notice to the Election Commission on 26 October on a petition against deletions in Maharashtra's revision and listed it for 5 November, and the Chief Justice orally assured that no elector deleted in the revision would be prosecuted for applying again through Form 6, The Hindu and LawChakra reported. The Bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana declined to extend the period for claims and objections, which closed that day, or to stop the final roll before hearing the Commission. Senior advocate Arvind Datar, for the petitioner, said thousands of electors in Mumbai and Pune were marked absent and then deleted because their old buildings were being redeveloped and they had moved out, and he put the redevelopment projects at 3,500 in Mumbai and 1,500 in Pune. He said electors who had been deleted were being made to file Form 6 as new voters, which he said is an offence, and asked for a new form to be notified for electors deleted in the revision. LawChakra reported that he also said about 3 crore of the state's roughly 9 crore electors had been deleted after the draft, 1.22 crore of them for a logical discrepancy, and that about 40% were missing from the rolls in Pune and Mumbai. ANI reported the Chief Justice as saying the Court could extend the date later if it found people who had yet to file their documents.

items.case: A petition seeking a writ of quo warranto against the Chief Election Commissioner, on which notice was issued on 5 October 2026, heard with W.P.(Crl.) No. 401 of 2026, Supreme Court
items.headline: No change to Form 6; members' approval obtained electronically in urgent matters: ECI to Supreme Court
items.claim: The Election Commission filed a short affidavit in the Supreme Court on 26 October in reply to a petition seeking a writ of quo warranto against the Chief Election Commissioner over how the Commission's decisions are taken, and said the affidavit was approved by a unanimous decision of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, Bar and Bench reported. The affidavit says files go to one Election Commissioner, then to the other and then to the Chief Election Commissioner, and that a suggestion, observation or query by a member during this process is not a decision of the Commission under Section 18 of the 2023 Act. It says that in urgent cases members approve electronically and the approval is recorded on the file later. It says the three SIR orders of 24 June 2025, 27 October 2025 and 14 May 2026 were unanimous decisions of the Commission. It says Form 6 has not been amended, because only the Central Government can amend it, and that the SIR declaration is a separate document. It accepts that the way the declaration was shown online could be read as an amendment, and says this was done so that an applicant needs a single OTP and e-sign. By a decision of the Commission's ER Division of 21 October 2026 the online application is to be in two parts, as the paper forms are. It says the appeals in West Bengal against the inclusion of electors were filed by officers of the state Chief Electoral Officer under the Court's orders and were not placed before the Commission. It says the Commission decided on 26 September 2026 that Booth Level Officers will collect documents from the homes of unmapped electors, who need not be called to a hearing, and that hearings will be held only in exceptional cases, preferably online. Item iii of the Commission's press note ECI/PN/120/2026 of 26 September 2026 reads "The declaration attached to Form 6 for SIR has been upheld by the Hon’ble Supreme Court." The affidavit, as Bar and Bench reported it, says the SIR declaration is a separate document. LiveLaw reported that the petitions were listed before the bench of the Chief Justice, Justice Bagchi and Justice Mohana on 27 October. The Indian Express, which reported the affidavit on 27 October, said it was approved for filing by a unanimous decision of all three members and reported further points. The affidavit accepts that the way the declaration appeared online "could be construed as though an amendment of Form 6 had been made" and that "certain steps taken by the officers" needed "to be corrected". It says the Electoral Registration Officer remains the statutory authority for the roll and that "no entry is added or deleted or modified except by order of the Electoral Registration Officer". It sets out a committee that includes experts from IIT Mumbai and IISc Bengaluru to review whether ECINet complies with the law, as decided by the Commission on 26 and 30 September, and the scrutiny of new IT modules before they are approved. It says 88 of the 97 Goa electors left off the final roll have since applied through Form 6. It says the West Bengal appeals were filed by officers in the state Chief Electoral Officer's office, citing a letter from that office of 22 October. It says an order by which a senior officer redistributed work among the Commission's officers was never implemented after the two Election Commissioners' joint direction, and that the letters the two Commissioners wrote were about that order.

items.response: This is the Commission's own account, given on oath. The Commission filed a short reply because of the Dussehra vacation and asked for liberty to file a detailed reply paragraph by paragraph. The affidavit does not say how many West Bengal appeals were filed, who in the Chief Electoral Officer's office approved them, or on what grounds, Bar and Bench reported. It says the affidavit presents the ECINet committee as the Commission's decision of September without mentioning Election Commissioner Vivek Joshi's proposal of 29 May, does not explain why Goa's registration officers could not act on their decisions in the software in February, and does not reconcile its West Bengal account with Election Commissioner Sukhbir Singh Sandhu's note that the state's Chief Electoral Officer told him she had no information about the appeals. On the July order, the paper says the affidavit does not say why it was issued without the Commission, why the file was withheld from a member of the Commission, or what has happened to the officer, who is not named.

items.case: The petition of two transparency activists on the Delhi SIR, W.P.(C) No. 1188 of 2026, and their application on Form 6 (court-30, court-48), Supreme Court
items.headline: Delhi SIR : Why Deleted Voters Asked To File Form 6 When They Were On 2026 Rolls? Supreme Court Asks ECI
items.claim: The bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana asked the Election Commission on 28 October why electors left off Delhi's draft for not returning enumeration forms are asked to apply on Form 6, which is meant for first-time voters, when they were on the roll of 2026, LiveLaw reported. Justice Bagchi said the Commission's four categories leave no place for electors who were never served a form, such as someone away from Delhi for a month, and that if the roll of 2026 is the base an elector who has shifted should be allowed Form 8. The bench suggested a residual category for those temporarily away, asked the Commission to reach out to electors given Delhi's floating population, and, as Bar and Bench reported, said the excluded names must be easily accessible in simple Hindi and local languages. Bar and Bench also reported Justice Bagchi saying the Court had not finally decided whether the logical discrepancy exercise is lawful, and had allowed it in West Bengal only as an interim arrangement. Counsel for the petitioners, Prashant Bhushan, said 43 of the 47 lakh left off are shown as permanently shifted or absent. The Indian Express reported that the bench said electors left off the draft who had only been away for a time should be allowed to submit the enumeration form, and those who had moved to another address in Delhi should be allowed Form 8. The Chief Justice suggested a statement or circular saying that Form 6 is to be filled only by those registering as voters in Delhi for the first time, LiveLaw and The Indian Express reported, and The Indian Express reported him adding that it was not for those on the roll of 2026 who could not fill the enumeration form because they had moved or were away. Hindustan Times reported the Court asking for a public notice saying that Form 6 is for first-time enrolment and that those who had moved could use Form 8 or the enumeration form. The Chief Justice also told the Commission not to go by any cut-off date while no election is due in Delhi, to keep inviting Form 6 and Form 8 and verify the documents attached, and to issue a public notice in newspapers and online that the process is continuing, The Indian Express reported. The Times of India reported the bench's suggestion that the Commission publish the list of electors left off with the reason against each name, ask them to contact the nearest booth level officer and fill Form 8, give them enumeration forms and tell them they may fill either Form 6 or Form 8. The bench listed the matter after two weeks. The Indian Express reported that the bench said it was not issuing an order to extend the deadline of 30 October and expected the Commission to act on its own, and The Times of India reported that the bench spoke without passing any order. No written order was reported. Anjali Bhardwaj, one of the two petitioners, wrote on X on 30 October that the Court had said electors on the list of absent, shifted, dead and duplicate electors should be allowed to fill the enumeration form or Form 8 in place of Form 6, which she wrote requires them to make a false declaration that they are first-time voters. She wrote that 32 lakh of the 47 lakh on that list in Delhi were marked permanently shifted and 12 lakh untraceable or absent.
items.quote: In Bihar, the Election Commission had not initially undertaken logical discrepancy as a category. We permitted it as an interim arrangement in West Bengal. We have not finally adjudicated upon the legality of the logical discrepancy exercise,
items.response: Senior Advocate Dama Seshadri Naidu, for the Commission, said the authorities would examine the concerns, take remedial steps and consider extending the deadline, LiveLaw reported. He said the roll of 2026 before the revision is the base. Bar and Bench reported that the Commission would consider accepting late enumeration forms and would extend the deadline of 30 October if needed. The Indian Express reported Naidu telling the bench that the Commission would report its steps in two weeks and that the time would be extended in the meanwhile. The Times of India reported him saying that the Commission had held more than one lakh camps in Delhi, that not a single person had come to fill Form 8, and that no one had been prosecuted for using Form 6 to restore a name.

items.case: Appeals by the Election Commission before West Bengal's SIR appellate tribunals in Samserganj and Sujapur (court-47)
items.headline: Two Bengal Seats, 72,000 ECI Appeals, One Timestamp: 99% of Target Voters Are Muslim
items.claim: In Sujapur, in Malda district, the Election Commission has filed appeals against the inclusion of 61,066 of the 1,07,690 electors whom judicial officers examined and found eligible, 56.7%, The Wire reported. It said that is more appeals than in any other seat in West Bengal. The figures come from appeal records collected by the Civic Research Group. In Samserganj, in Murshidabad district, judicial officers found 74,775 electors not eligible, the most of any seat, and the Commission has appealed against 15,195 of the 33,152 they cleared, 47.6%. The Wire reported that 72,838 of the 76,156 pending appeals in the two seats, 96%, carry one timestamp of 5 April 2026, two days before the roll was frozen for the Assembly election, and that their numbers run in sequence one roll part at a time, which it reads as appeals generated in batches. It reported that 99.9% of the electors appealed against in Samserganj and 99.6% in Sujapur have names it describes as recognisably Muslim, a classification it says it estimated from Bengali names and not from official records. It said the Commission did not single them out from among those cleared, because almost everyone the judges cleared in both seats has such a name. The tribunals had decided 105 of the 76,261 appeals in the two seats. In Sujapur the appeals equal almost a quarter of the draft roll of 2,56,276 and slightly exceed the winning margin of 60,287 in April, and in Samserganj they are about twice the margin of 7,587.
items.quote: Of these 76,156 appeals in total, 72,838, or 96%, share a single timestamp on April 5, 2026.
items.response: The report says the Commission has not said on what grounds it is challenging these electors, whether each case was reviewed before an appeal was filed, why so many appeals share one timestamp, or why it has appealed against about half or more of those cleared. No reply from the Commission is reported.

items.case: Petitions on the Kerala SIR, heard with the SIR matters concerning Uttar Pradesh and Chhattisgarh (up-26), Supreme Court

items.case: Appeals by the Election Commission before West Bengal's SIR appellate tribunals against electors cleared by judicial officers (court-47, court-55)
items.headline: Bengal SIR Observer Says He Knew Nothing About CEO Office's 16 Lakh Appeals Against Cleared Voters
items.claim: Subrata Gupta, the Election Commission's special roll observer for West Bengal's revision, told The Wire that the observers had no information that the Chief Electoral Officer's office had filed appeals against electors whom judicial officers had examined and found eligible. He said the observers' role ended with the supplementary rolls, which listed about 33 lakh electors the judicial officers retained and 27 lakh they deleted, that he had heard that many of the 27 lakh deleted had appealed for inclusion and that the observers had no access to those records, and that they had heard of the appeals against inclusion only informally, with no official communication. The Commission told the Supreme Court in September that 16,10,311 such appeals had been filed. Its counter affidavit of 26 October (court-52) said a letter of 22 October from the Chief Electoral Officer's office stated that the office's officers had filed them as authorities under the Representation of the People Act. The Wire reported that Gupta, a retired IAS officer of the 1990 batch, now advises Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari.
items.quote: So, when you say that such a large number of appeals have been filed, that is information we are now receiving. We had no information about these appeals being filed or having been filed.
items.response: The Wire says it has written to the Chief Electoral Officer and the Additional Chief Electoral Officer of West Bengal asking which officers filed the appeals, on whose decision and on what grounds. No reply is reported.
items.note: By Aparna Bhattacharya in The Wire, published 30 October 2026 at 11:31 am IST (post_date_gmt 06:01:20), read in full through The Wire's CMS API (posts/detail) on 30 October 2026. The report also cites Election Commissioner Sukhbir Singh Sandhu's file note of 12 August, as quoted in a petition before the Supreme Court, asking who was authorised to file the appeals, and The Indian Express's report that Sandhu said neither he, Vivek Joshi nor the state's Chief Electoral Officer knew the basis of the appeals. items.case: Appeals by the Election Commission before West Bengal's SIR appellate tribunals in Hemtabad (court-47, court-55)
items.headline: In One Bengal Seat, EC Appealed Against 599 Voters Even Before Their Adjudication Result Was Published
items.claim: In Hemtabad, a seat reserved for Scheduled Castes in Uttar Dinajpur district, the Election Commission has filed appeals against 15,381 of the 34,327 electors whom judicial officers examined and found eligible, 44.8%, The Wire reported from appeal records collected by the Civic Research Group, which it says it analysed and verified again. Of the 13,776 pending appeals, 12,758 carry the code the activists read as the batch lodged on the evening of 5 April 2026, 978 the code for 6 April, and 40 were filed online. The paper reported that 599 of the appeals with the 5 April code concern electors cleared in the constituency's twelfth and last supplementary list, which was published on 6 April, so the appeals were on record before the list that cleared those electors was made public. The 599 come from nine polling stations, and 162 of them from part 237. Of the 2,65,162 electors on Hemtabad's draft roll, 52,542 were placed under adjudication, and judicial officers struck off 18,215 and found 34,327 eligible. The Wire reported that at least 97.7% of the electors appealed against, and all 599, have Muslim names, which largely mirrors the 97% of all those cleared, and that the Commission's appeal rate in the seat is close to its statewide rate of 49.4%. The tribunals have marked 1,605 of the seat's appeals disposed of.
items.quote: For 599 of those voters, the appeal came before their clearance had even been made public.
items.response: The report says the records cannot show whether the judicial officers' decisions were already on the Commission's portal before the list was published. The Commission told the Supreme Court on 26 October that officers of the office of the West Bengal Chief Electoral Officer filed the appeals (court-52), and the report says it has not said which officers or on what grounds. items.case: Reference of electors to judicial officers in West Bengal's revision under the Supreme Court's orders (court-57, soft-42)
items.headline: How Over 50 Lakh Cleared West Bengal Voters Ended Up Under Judicial Review In SIR
items.claim: The Election Commission's statewide Notice and Hearing Report dated 22 February, seen by The Wire, records that when the deadline for deciding hearing cases passed on 21 February, West Bengal's Electoral Registration Officers and their assistants had cleared 1,31,45,109 of 1,51,92,634 cases for the final roll, 86.5%, found 11,58,636 ineligible, 7.6%, and left 8,88,889 undecided, 5.9%, The Wire reported. The final roll of 28 February placed 60,06,675 electors under adjudication, and The Wire says at least 51 lakh of them had already been decided by a registration officer. In the report the Electoral Roll Micro Observers marked 31,43,868 cases 'documents need to be reviewed' and the roll observers marked 40,28,055, some of them the same cases. Where the registration officers acted on these flags they disagreed with the observers in 35,92,292 cases and agreed in 2,02,926. Across the 24 districts The Wire finds that the number placed under adjudication rises and falls with the observers' flags, with a correlation of 0.95, and bears little relation to the cases left undecided, with a correlation of 0.26. In Malda 8,730 cases were left undecided and 8,28,127 electors were placed under adjudication, and in Murshidabad the figures were 12,194 and 11,01,145. In Uttar Dinajpur 4,80,341 were placed under adjudication against 2,75,074 observer flags.
items.quote: The commission’s own deadline report shows that EROs had left only about 8.9 lakh cases undecided, against 60 lakh sent to judges.
items.response: The Wire quotes the Chief Electoral Officer's office as saying on 1 March that names were marked under adjudication 'since the concerned EROs/AEROs did not decide them after hearing'. Subrata Gupta, the Commission's special roll observer, told it that the Commission had told observers that about 90 lakh of about 1.5 crore cases heard had been disposed of and 60 lakh were pending. The Wire says it has sent the Chief Electoral Officer queries on who decided to send cases the registration officers had already decided to the judges, and that it will update the report on a reply.
items.note: By Aparna Bhattacharya in The Wire, Kolkata, published 2 November 2026 at 9:05 pm IST (post_date_gmt 15:35:43), read in full through The Wire's CMS API (posts/detail) with curl on 3 November 2026. The report is not published with the Notice and Hearing Report, and the figures are The Wire's reading of it. The three figures for cases cleared, found ineligible and left undecided add to the total. The figure of 51 lakh is The Wire's, and the report does not show which individual electors were sent to the judges, as The Wire says. The 60,06,675 under adjudication and the 27.16 lakh judicial officers later deleted are already on the site. The Supreme Court's order of 9 February, which The Wire quotes as saying the final decision will be taken by the registration officers only, and the Commission's counter affidavit of 26 October (court-52), are quoted in the report as background. Not carried: the photograph of a polling station's screen in Satgachhia shared by a booth level officer, who is a private person, the religion of the electors in that part, the margin by which the seat was won in April, and the roll observers' correlation of 0.97. The Wire's earlier reports on Murshidabad and Nadia from ERONET are soft-42, and the special roll observer's account of the appeals is court-57.

items.outlet: Letter of the petitioners to the Chief Election Commissioner, and ECI letter No. 23/2026-ERS (Vol.-II), both of 03.11.2026, as Prashant Bhushan posted them on X
items.case: The petition of Anjali Bhardwaj and Amrita Johri on the Delhi SIR, W.P.(C) No. 1188 of 2026, and IA No. 317050 of 2026, Supreme Court (court-54)
items.headline: The petitioners in the Delhi case ask the Commission to accept Form 8 and enumeration forms, and the Commission clarifies Form 6 the same day
items.claim: Anjali Bhardwaj and Amrita Johri, the two transparency activists who are the petitioners in the Supreme Court case on Delhi's revision, wrote to the Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, on 3 November 2026, with a copy to Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer, Ashok Kumar, asking for immediate compliance with what they call the Court's directives at the hearing of 28 October (court-54). Their letter says the bench observed that forcing voters "deleted during SIR" to fill Form 6, which contains the declaration of being a first-time voter, is an error, and that the judges termed it a "structural incongruity". It says that of the 47 lakh electors left off Delhi's draft and placed on the list of absent, shifted, dead and duplicate electors, 31.59 lakh were marked permanently shifted and 11.73 lakh untraceable or absent. The letter says the Court orally directed that those marked as having shifted residence be allowed to fill Form 8, and said that the 11.73 lakh marked absent or untraceable should be allowed to fill enumeration forms even at this stage and not be forced to enrol as new voters on Form 6. It asks the Commission and Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer to set up and publicise a simple way to do this, with clear instructions to accept Form 8 and enumeration forms from electors on the list without making them submit Form 6, and it notes that the Commission has extended Delhi's timeline. On the same day the Commission wrote to the Chief Electoral Officers of every state and union territory that an elector whose name is not in the draft roll has to seek inclusion afresh, may do so on Form 6, and is not to face action under section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 only because the elector was on an earlier roll, provided the elector is not enrolled in any other constituency and the declaration is otherwise in accordance with law. The Commission's letter does not mention Form 8, the enumeration form, the petitioners' letter or the Supreme Court hearing. Prashant Bhushan, counsel for the petitioners, posted both letters on X on 3 November and wrote that "in response to our letter asking EC to allow shifted votes to fill form 8, the ECI issued orders to force shifted voters to fill form 6 (with an assurance that they will not be prosecuted for false declaration)". The Hindu reported both letters the same day.
items.quote: Clear instructions should be issued to accept Form 8/enumeration forms from voters on the ASDD list without forcing them to submit Form 6, which contains the declaration of being a first-time voter.
items.response: The Commission's letter No. 23/2026-ERS (Vol.-II) of 3 November 2026 says: "The submission of Form 6 in such circumstances is, therefore, for the purpose of inclusion in the electoral roll under SIR or afterwards and is not, by itself, false merely because the elector was previously enrolled." It cites the Delhi High Court's order of 14 October 2026 (court-45) and names no other court proceeding.
items.note: Both letters were read in full from the four images of Prashant Bhushan's post on X (https://x.com/pbhushan1/status/2117642820588810572, 3 November 2026, 15:39 UTC, 9:09 pm IST), fetched through api.fxtwitter.com on 4 November 2026: the petitioners' letter on two pages (page 1 of 2 and the signature page) and the Commission's letter on two pages, signed by Sandeep Kumar, Under Secretary. The Commission's letter was read again in full from the PDF India TV hosts (https://getapi.indiatvnews.com/doc/clarification-on-form-6.pdf, 2 pages, SHA-256 71d5d118...aceee6a5, curl on 4 November 2026), whose text matches the images word for word, with a copy list to the Commission's officers that the images do not show. The Hindu, by Sreeparna Chakrabarty, published 3 November 2026, 8:16 pm IST, updated 10:52 pm, read from the JSON-LD articleBody with curl on 4 November 2026, reports both letters. Its text says the Commission spoke on Tuesday, November 2, and the letter is dated 3 November 2026, a Tuesday. The petitioners' letter cites the CEO Delhi's FAQ on the SIR 2026, question 30, which says an elector not living at the registered address will not get an enumeration form, will be left off the draft as permanently shifted, and may file Form 6 with the declaration form during claims and objections. The letter's 31.59 lakh and 11.73 lakh are The Hindu's counts of 2 September 2026 from the Chief Electoral Officer's booth-wise lists, which data/india/states.json already carries for Delhi. The letter calls the electors deleted. They were left off the draft, and the claim says so. The Commission's letter names the two petitioners in the Delhi High Court case, who are private persons and are not named here, as in court-45. Bhushan's post wrote "shifted votes" where the sense is shifted voters, and the quote keeps his words. His reading that the Commission's letter answers the petitioners' letter is his. The Commission's letter does not refer to it. Not carried: the post of the Congress's account and the post of Jairam Ramesh (https://x.com/Jairam_Ramesh/status/2117646076853604765, 3 November 2026), which are commentary. Ramesh's post also says the Maharashtra Chief Electoral Officer wrote to the Commission that Form 6 cannot be used in this way, and that the Goa Bench of the Bombay High Court has questioned the Commission's reasoning. Neither was read from a source here.

items.case: The petition of Anjali Bhardwaj and Amrita Johri on the Delhi SIR, W.P.(C) No. 1188 of 2026, Supreme Court (court-54, court-60)
items.headline: SIR: Don’t fear, Supreme Court tells Delhi voters struck off draft electoral roll
items.claim: Prashant Bhushan, counsel for the petitioners in the Delhi case, mentioned the matter before a bench of the Chief Justice, Surya Kant, on 4 November and said electors left off the draft feared prosecution if they filed Form 6 with its declaration that they were enrolling for the first time, although the Commission's letter of 3 November says no action will be taken on that ground alone (court-60), Hindustan Times and The Hindu reported. He said the letter went against what the Court had said at the hearing of 28 October (court-54), and that the Commission had extended the time for claims and objections in Delhi to 25 November. The Chief Justice asked how electors could be afraid when the Court was hearing the matter, told the petitioners to file an application, and said the Court would hear it on 19 November, the date the matter is already listed for. The Court passed no urgent order. The Hindu reports that the Chief Justice said the case would be heard after the Deepavali holidays, and that the bench said the Commission could be asked to extend the date further if required.
items.quote: How can they feel afraid like this when we are hearing the matter? You can file your application. The matter is already listed on November 19. We will hear it that day.
items.response: The Commission's letter No. 23/2026-ERS (Vol.-II) of 3 November 2026 says no action under section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 is to be started against an elector only because the elector was on an earlier roll and filed Form 6, provided the elector is not enrolled in another constituency (court-60). Neither report gives anything said for the Commission at the mentioning.
items.note: Hindustan Times, by Abraham Thomas, published 4 November 2026, 12:52 pm IST, read in full from the JSON-LD articleBody with curl on 4 November 2026. The Hindu (The Hindu Bureau, published 4 November 2026, 12:17 pm IST, modified 12:43 pm), read in full the same way, gives the same mentioning and the date of 19 November, and quotes Bhushan that the electors are 'in the horns of a dilemma'. Hindustan Times gives the Chief Justice's question to Bhushan whether the Commission's letter speaks of prosecution under section 31, and Bhushan's answer that it says there will be no prosecution but that voters are in a dilemma. Hindustan Times describes the hearing of 28 October as a direction to the Commission. court-54 records it as oral, with no written order, and that reading is kept. Its count of over 3.15 million electors who could be given Form 8 is the paper's own and is not carried. list-02 dates the next hearing to about 11 November, worked out from the Commission's two weeks for a report. Both reports of 4 November give 19 November, and list-06 carries that date. The petitioners are named as in court-60.

items.case: A petition by a group of advocates for guidelines on processions and protests near the Supreme Court, after the march of 12 October against the Chief Election Commissioner (court-44)
items.headline: SC seeks Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge’s replies on plea over Opposition march against CEC to top court
items.claim: A bench of the Chief Justice, Surya Kant, on 3 November sought replies from the Congress president, Mallikarjun Kharge, and Rahul Gandhi, and from the Centre, on a petition by a group of advocates about the Opposition's march to the Supreme Court on 12 October against the Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, and listed it for 23 November, Hindustan Times reported. The petition seeks guidelines regulating processions, protests, demonstrations and assemblies near the Court. For the petitioners, the senior advocate Gaurav Bhatia said the march drew a large gathering of lawyers and supporters into the court precincts, alleged that Gandhi pushed a woman journalist who was three months pregnant and that she had to be taken to hospital, and moved an application for an FIR against Gandhi. The Solicitor General, Tushar Mehta, said the Centre would reply by the next date and asked that the matter be heard with a petition by the Network of Women in Media, India on the harassment of women journalists covering protests in Delhi. The petition also names Akhilesh Yadav, the Delhi Commissioner of Police, the Supreme Court registry and the Congress as respondents.
items.quote: The plea is seeking guidelines regulating processions, protests, demonstrations and assemblies in the vicinity of the top court.
items.response: The senior advocate Abhishek Manu Singhvi, for Gandhi and Kharge, said their replies would be filed soon and asked that "irresponsible statements should not be made before the court takes up the matter".
items.note: Hindustan Times, by Abraham Thomas, published 3 November 2026, 4:15 pm IST (modified 4:27 pm), read in full from the JSON-LD articleBody with curl on 4 November 2026. The Court issued notice on the same petition on 15 October (court-44). LiveLaw's report of that hearing names the same lead petitioner and three other advocates, and Gaurav Bhatia as their counsel, which is how the two are matched. The lead petitioner, an advocate named in the report, and the journalist are private persons and are not named here. The allegation about the journalist is the petitioners' counsel's, made in court, and the report carries no answer to it beyond Singhvi's request. No second report of the hearing of 3 November was found. The next date is list-07.

items.outlet: Bombay High Court at Goa (judgment of 5.11.2026, as published by LiveLaw)
items.case: Writ Petition No. 732 of 2026, a family's petition on deletion after Form 8, Bombay High Court at Goa
items.headline: Bombay High Court at Goa orders a Santa Cruz family of six onto the roll within ten days and refuses the Commission a stay
items.claim: The Bombay High Court at Goa on 5 November allowed the petition of a family of six from Santa Cruz who had moved house within the constituency, filed Form 8 and were left off the draft roll and the final roll (court-32, court-33, court-41). A bench of Justices Valmiki Menezes and Amit S. Jamsandekar held that section 22 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 and rule 13 of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 stay in force during a special intensive revision, and that a registration officer who receives Form 8 is bound to decide it. It held that the family were not new voters and could not be told to file Form 6. It also held that Form 6, the pre-filled enumeration form and the declaration in Annexure D to the guidelines would each have made them give a false declaration open to prosecution under section 31. The registration officer rejected their Form 8 on 21 January 2026, two days after claims and objections closed, with no formal order, no reasons and no hearing. The court found that the only reason was that ERONET was frozen during enumeration and gave the officer one option, which was to reject. It held that this amounted to a suspension of section 22 and rule 13 and was impermissible. It allowed the petition against the rejection and the two appeal orders that upheld it, and directed the registration officer of Santa Cruz to include the six in Part 25 of the roll within ten days, after confirming their residence. It made no order as to costs. It declined to keep the petition pending until the Supreme Court decides the challenges to the revision, because the family had not challenged the revision itself. The Times of India reported on 13 November that the six were back on the roll of Santa Cruz with their original EPIC numbers, and that Goa's Chief Electoral Officer, Sanjay Goel, said they had been included in the draft roll published on 12 November, as the court directed.
items.quote: We reject any contention of the Election Commission that during the process of a Special Intensive Revision, the ERO is within the law to refuse giving effect to Form 8 whilst the revision is underway. ... Removal of a name of an elector from the revised Roll, specially when they have already submitted Form 8 for shifting of residence within the same constituency, as has been done by the Petitioners, and that too without affording them any hearing would amount to denial of the citizen’s right to vote.
items.response: For the Commission, Gaurish Agni and, at later hearings, the senior advocate Ashutosh Kumbhakoni argued that the family's Form 8 was rightly rejected because they had refused to fill the pre-filled enumeration form and hand it to the booth level officer at their old address, that they were new voters in relation to the draft roll and had to file Form 6 with the Annexure D declaration, and that the portal for processing forms was frozen during enumeration. After the judgment was pronounced the Commission's advocate, Gaurish Agni, asked for a stay of at least two weeks so that the Commission could challenge it in the Supreme Court. The bench refused because its directions concern including the petitioners in the roll. Dainik Gomantak TV reported on 6 November that Agni said the Commission is moving the Supreme Court against the order. The Times of India reported on 13 November that one of the six had filed a caveat in the Supreme Court, in anticipation of an appeal by the Commission, so that no stay would be passed without his being heard. It did not report an appeal by the Commission. Goa's Chief Electoral Officer, Sanjay Goel, told O Heraldo his office would study the order, implement it if it could be implemented, and challenge it if there was scope to.
items.note: Judgment of Justices Valmiki Menezes and Amit S. Jamsandekar (per Menezes J.) in Writ Petition No. 732 of 2026, reserved on 13 October and pronounced on 5 November 2026, neutral citation 2026:BHC-GOA:2366-DB, CNR HCBM050020712026, 42 pages, read in full from the PDF LiveLaw published on 5 November, fetched with curl on 6 November 2026. The direction and 'no order as to costs' are in paragraph 44, and the request for a stay of at least two weeks and its refusal in paragraph 45. The respondents are the State of Goa, the Chief Electoral Officer, the North Goa District Election Officer, and the registration officer and assistant registration officer of 13 St. Cruz. Gaurish Agni appeared through video conference with Ashutosh Kumbhakoni, and Vivek Rodrigues for the family. The judgment dates the family's Form 8 to 12 November 2025 through the BLO, uploaded on 8 December 2025, with enumeration ending on 11 December, the draft on 16 December, claims and objections closing on 19 January 2026 and the rejection by SMS on 21 January. The District Election Officer's appeal order is of 2 March 2026 and the Chief Electoral Officer's of 16 April 2026. The assistant registration officer's letter of 20 February 2026, as the judgment gives it, dates the processing after the draft to 16.05.2025 in paragraph 33 and 16.12.2026 in paragraph 42, which appear to be misprints for 16 December 2025. The Commission's statement that it will go to the Supreme Court is from a screenshot of a Dainik Gomantak TV post on Facebook, posted about seven hours before 07:49 IST on 6 November, which gives it as Agni's words. In court the stay was sought 'to permit Election Commission of India to assail correctness of this Judgment before the Hon’ble Supreme Court', and India Today, Bar and Bench, PTI in Deccan Herald, The Goan and O Heraldo report the request and the refusal. Bar and Bench (Neha Joshi, 5 November) gives the bench's words from the pronouncement as 'No stay. How can we grant stay on including names of voters in the list! You get a stay from Supreme Court', and The Goan gives the same with small differences. Goel's words are from O Heraldo (Team Herald, 6 November). Hindustan Times (Gerard de Souza) quotes him at more length. Also read with curl: The Indian Express (Pavneet Singh Chadha), Times of India (Lisa Monteiro), PTI in The Economic Times and Rediff, India Today (Vidya), LiveLaw (Narsi Benwal, 6 November) and Hindustan Times. The Goan says the court directed the Chief Electoral Officer, and the judgment directs the registration officer, respondent 4. Rediff calls the judgment 44 pages and the PDF has 42. No report in The Hindu or The Navhind Times was found by a search on 6 November. The judgment and every report name the family, and the item does not. Update, 13 November 2026: The Times of India (Lisa Monteiro, Panaji, published 13 November 2026 at 12:02 am IST, datePublished 2026-11-13T00:02:00+05:30) was read in full from the JSON-LD articleBody with curl on 13 November 2026. It gives Goel's statement that the six were included in the draft roll published on Thursday, which was 12 November, the day of Goa's draft roll in the special summary revision, and reports that they were included with their original EPIC numbers. It reports that the head of the family filed the caveat, in his own name, and does not date it. Gomantak TV and Goa News Hub posts on Facebook and Instagram that report the caveat were seen only as search results and were not read. The report names the family, and the item does not.

items.case: Petitions by Manoj Jha and an advocate challenging section 16 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, Supreme Court
items.headline: SC seeks Centre, EC response on law giving blanket, lifelong immunity to CEC, Election Commissioners
items.claim: A bench of the Chief Justice, Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana issued notice to the Centre and the Election Commission on 4 November on petitions challenging section 16 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, and listed them for 18 December, The Hindu and The Indian Express reported. Section 16 bars every court from entertaining or continuing any civil or criminal proceedings against a serving or former Chief Election Commissioner or Election Commissioner for any act, thing or word in the discharge of official duty. The Hindu reports that the petitions were filed by the RJD Member of Parliament Manoj Jha and by an advocate. The petitions argue that the section bars the jurisdiction of the constitutional courts and interferes with judicial review, which has been held to be part of the basic structure of the Constitution. The advocate's plea, as The Hindu quotes it, says the section bars all kinds of prosecution, gives immunity for life and covers acts that may be outside lawful authority. The petitions point out that the President and the Governors are protected from criminal proceedings only while in office. The advocate's plea, as The Indian Express quotes it, says a voter whose name is wrongly deleted from the roll is left without a remedy, and it cites the paper's reports of alleged differences between the Chief Election Commissioner and the two Election Commissioners over the SIR. The Indian Express reports that the Court is already hearing a petition by the NGO Lok Prahari against the same section, in which it issued notice in January and declined to stay the section.
items.quote: A voter whose name is wrongly deleted from the electoral roll, a candidate prejudiced by a mala fide act, and any citizen aggrieved by corruption in the functioning of the Commission are left without a remedy.
items.response: Neither report gives anything said for the Centre or the Commission at the hearing. The advocate's plea says the section was added to the Bill by an amendment that gave no reasons for it, and that the Minister's justification in Parliament did not show it was needed.
items.note: The Hindu, by Krishnadas Rajagopal, published 4 November 2026, 1:43 pm IST (modified 1:44 pm), and The Indian Express (Express News Service, published 4 November 2026, 6:57 pm IST, modified 5 November, 4:09 am), both read in full from the JSON-LD articleBody with curl on 6 November 2026. The Hindu gives the two petitions, their counsel, the listing on 18 December and the comparison with Article 361. The Indian Express gives the bench of three, describes only the advocate's petition and calls it a fresh plea, and reports the earlier Lok Prahari petition and the plea's reference to its own reports on the Commission. The advocate is a private petitioner and is given by role, although both reports name him. The plea's reference to allegations about the Chief Election Commissioner's earlier service in Kerala is not carried. The next date is list-08.

items.case: Appeals by the Election Commission before West Bengal's SIR appellate tribunals against electors cleared by judicial officers (court-47, court-55, court-58)
items.headline: 9 in 10 Voters the Election Commission Wants Removed From Bengal’s Rolls Have Muslim Names
items.claim: The Wire's classification of the names in appeal records compiled by the Civic Research Group finds that at least 14,39,797 of the 16,08,175 electors against whose inclusion the Election Commission has appealed, after judicial officers examined them and found them eligible, have Muslim names, 89.5%. The report gives Muslims as 27% of West Bengal's population in the 2011 Census and about 29% of its electorate. Grouping seats by the minority share of their population, The Wire finds Muslim names among 61.7% of the electors appealed against in the 89 seats where that share is under 10%, 83.8% in the 71 seats at 10% to 20%, 90.3% in the 51 seats at 20% to 30%, 93.8% in the 39 seats at 30% to 50% and 96.6% in the 41 seats over 50%. In every group the Commission appealed against between 46.5% and 51.2% of the electors the judges cleared, and the report says that across seats there is almost no relationship between a seat's Muslim share and the share of its cleared electors appealed against. It counts 137 constituencies where at least 90% of the electors appealed against have Muslim names, and 2,62,416 electors with Muslim names facing appeals in the 160 seats where Muslims are under a fifth of the population. In Purba Medinipur district, where it gives the Muslim share of the population as 12.0%, 92.9% of the 27,091 electors appealed against have Muslim names, and in Purba Bardhaman, at 23.3%, 95.9% of 90,637 do. In Murshidabad the figure is 98.2%. In Krishnaganj in Nadia, a seat reserved for Scheduled Castes, Muslim names are 157 of the 2,412 electors appealed against, 6.5%, against a population share of 5.7%, and in Jadavpur they are 125 of 881, 14.2%, against 1.2%. The report also uses a second set of records, of appeals by electors whom judicial officers deleted, and does not say who compiled them. It counts 22,17,619 such appellants among the 27,06,057 deleted, 82%, and finds Muslim names among 79.3% of them. The two sets of records cover 38,25,794 of the 59,59,458 electors sent to judicial officers in these constituencies, and The Wire counts 31,99,122 of them with Muslim names, which it says means that at least 53.7% of all those sent to adjudication had Muslim names even if none of the others did. In the seats under 10%, it finds Muslim names among about a third of the deleted electors who appealed and among 61.7% of the cleared electors the Commission appealed against.
items.quote: Nine in every ten West Bengal voters whom the Election Commission of India (ECI) is seeking to remove from the electoral rolls, even after judicial officers have found them eligible, have Muslim names.
items.response: The Wire says it has written to the office of West Bengal's Chief Electoral Officer and two Additional Chief Electoral Officers asking which officers filed the appeals, under what provision officers of that office can appeal against electors in constituencies they do not administer, whether registration officers were consulted, on what grounds and by what criteria electors were chosen, and whether each case was reviewed. It has also asked for the letter of 22 October that the Commission cites in its affidavit. It says the report will be updated when the office replies. The Commission's counter affidavit of 26 October (court-52), as the report quotes it, says officers of the Chief Electoral Officer's office filed the appeals as authorities under the Representation of the People Act and that the matters were not brought to the Commission. No reply from the Commission is reported.
items.note: By Aparna Bhattacharya in The Wire, Kolkata, published 9 November 2026 at 2:00 pm IST (post_date_gmt 08:30:12), read in full through The Wire's CMS API (posts/detail) with curl on 9 November 2026. The classification of names as Muslim is The Wire's, and its three charts carry the line 'Religion estimated from names, not official records'. The charts are The Wire's own, made from the appeal records, and none is a primary document. They take the minority share of each seat and district from what they call the SIR master list. The five groups of seats cover 291 seats and 15,90,534 appeals, 17,641 fewer than the statewide 16,08,175, which the report does not explain. The district chart says Kalimpong is left out because the master list gives it no minority share. The shares of the five groups weighted by their counts give about 14,40,000 Muslim names, which agrees with the statewide figure, and the 160 seats under a fifth are the 89 and the 71 seats of the first two groups. The 16,08,175 appeals against 32,53,401 cleared electors are already in court-47. The site's West Bengal summary has 22,21,118 appeals by electors found not eligible, 3,499 more than the 22,17,619 in these records. The report cites the Sabar Institute's finding that 70.17% of the more than 27 lakh deleted from the list under adjudication were Muslim and 51% women, which is not carried. Also not carried are the district table's other rows (Paschim Medinipur, Bankura, Jalpaiguri, Hooghly, Cooch Behar and Paschim Bardhaman), the seats Egra, Chandipur, Kanthi Dakshin, Ramnagar, Sagar and Gosaba, the other four seats in the third table, and the table of electors sent to judges per 1,000. The report's reading that the pattern comes from the stages before the appeal draws on the Commission's ERONET data, which is court-59. The report's word for what the appeals seek is 'remove', and here they are appeals against inclusion. The appeal records were not checked against any other source.

items.case: Writ petition by residents of Maharashtra to quash 14 orders of the Election Commission and the Chief Election Commissioner, Bombay High Court, Kolhapur Bench
items.headline: Petition before Bombay High Court to quash orders by CEC Gyanesh Kumar, restore voters deleted in SIR
items.claim: Residents of Maharashtra filed a writ petition before the Kolhapur Bench of the Bombay High Court through the advocate Asim Sarode asking it to quash 14 administrative orders passed by the Election Commission and the Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, over the past ten months, Bar and Bench reported on 24 September. The petition relies on The Indian Express's report that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi objected to these decisions on at least 14 occasions, and says the objections concerned voter registration, deletion and restoration of names, the electoral roll database, the functioning of registration officers and software. It argues that the Commission did not act in accordance with section 18 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, and that the Chief Election Commissioner failed to discharge his duties faithfully, so that no protection can extend to his actions in office. It also challenges the changes made to Form 6 in July. It asks for the 14 orders to be quashed, for the revision in Maharashtra to be stayed, for every elector deleted in Maharashtra in the revision to be restored, for the Assembly elections due in the states where the revision was held to be postponed until rolls are prepared in accordance with law, and for a judicial committee headed by a retired High Court judge to inquire into the deletions and the blockages in the software. On 28 September a bench of Justices Sharmila Deshmukh and Neeraj Dhote declined Sarode's request to hear it that day or the next and listed it for 22 October, Bar and Bench reported. The bench asked what was urgent about it and what private right the petitioners held against the Commission, and Sarode replied that the petition was filed for voters who feel their rights are being infringed. No report of a hearing on 22 October or of any later order was found.
items.quote: "Is it a PIL? Since it's a writ petition, what private right do you have against the Election Commission?" the bench asked.
items.response: No reply from the Commission is reported. Pudhari and Lokmat report that the bench said the matter raised no urgent question of life or liberty and listed it in view of the court's workload. Sarode told a press conference reported by Saamana on 30 September that notice had been sent to the Commission before the hearing on 22 October. items.case: West Bengal's SIR appellate tribunals of retired judges (court-18)
items.headline: Bengal SIR tribunal sees another exit as retired judge Biswajit Basu resigns
items.claim: The retired Calcutta High Court judge Biswajit Basu resigned on 7 November as head of one of West Bengal's 19 SIR appellate tribunals, citing personal reasons, and sent his resignation to the High Court's Chief Justice, Ravindra Vithalrao Ghuge, The Indian Express, The Hindu, the Hindustan Times and The New Indian Express reported. He was one of the two tribunal heads hearing appeals from Murshidabad district, and The New Indian Express reports that he and Indrajit Chatterjee each had 11 of its 22 constituencies. The Times of India reports that Murshidabad had over 7.4 lakh appeals pending when the Commission reported to the Supreme Court in September. The reports count the resignations differently. The Hindu, the Hindustan Times, The New Indian Express and PTI, as The Times of India carried it, call him the fourth to resign, after the former Chief Justice of the Calcutta High Court T.S. Sivagnanam and the retired judges Ranjit Kumar Bag and Indrajit Chatterjee, and The Hindu says Sivagnanam was the first, in May 2026. The Telegraph also calls him the fourth and does not name the others. The Indian Express calls him the second within a month in one report and the third in another, and The Times of India's Kolkata edition calls him the third in seven months. Those three reports and The Telegraph say Chatterjee stayed on after the Commission promised to deal with his complaints about the commute and its portal. The Indian Express reports, from sources, that Basu was unhappy with the tribunal's infrastructure and its login procedures, and its second report says the requirement of Aadhaar to log in to the Commission's portal was the last straw. The Times of India's Kolkata edition reports that the tribunals have not been examining appeals since 21 September, because the judges refused to log in to a new portal the Commission introduced. The Telegraph reports that no order has been uploaded to the portal since then, because the judges refused to share their Aadhaar details. Basu also chairs the state government's Commission on Institutional Corruption.
items.quote: “I have resigned from my duties of SIR tribunals. The resignation is for personal reasons,” Basu said on Saturday.
items.response: An official of the Commission told PTI that with both judges hearing Murshidabad's appeals stepping down within a month, the disposal of appeals from Murshidabad had effectively come to a standstill, as The Times of India carried it. The Trinamool Congress leader and lawyer Baiswanor Chatterjee asked what use the tribunal was when its judges had heard very few appeals, and the state BJP spokesperson Sayantan Basu said there was no reason to read anything into the resignation, since Justice Basu heads the inquiry commission probing corruption cases and was probably unable to spare the time, the Hindustan Times reported. No report says who will hear the appeals he was hearing.

items.case: Writ - A No. 18007 of 2026, a petition by five assistant teachers in Saharanpur against their deployment as booth level officers, Allahabad High Court
items.headline: Allahabad High Court holds that the RTE Act permits teachers to be deployed as booth level officers
items.claim: Justice Vinod Diwakar of the Allahabad High Court on 2 November dismissed a writ petition by five assistant teachers of junior and senior basic schools in Saharanpur district, who asked to be detached from their duties as booth level officers. The teachers argued that nothing in the terms of their service allows BLO duty to be given to them, and that it is contrary to Article 21-A of the Constitution and the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009, because it takes teachers away from teaching. The court held that preparing and revising the roll is a statutory function under the Representation of the People Act, 1950, that under section 13CC of that Act state and local government staff employed on the roll are deemed to be on deputation to the Election Commission for that period, and that section 27 of the 2009 Act expressly permits teachers to be deployed for election duties, which include BLO duties. It found the argument on Article 21-A misconceived and said the teachers had not shown that their work as BLOs had harmed their teaching or the children's education. The judgment does not name the revision. The Hindustan Times and Bar and Bench report that the duties it covers include work in the SIR.
items.quote: Further, Section 27 of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009 expressly permits the deployment of teachers for election-related duties, and BLO duties fall within this exception. The submission based on Article 21-A and the RTE Rules is, therefore, misconceived.
items.response: The judgment records that the court heard the State's standing counsel and gives no submission for the State or the Commission. No reply from the teachers was reported.

items.case: Revision petition by the Banbhoolpura police against the Haldwani magistrate's order of 6 October to register an FIR over 28 Form 7s (form7-36), court of the First Additional Sessions Judge

items.claim: The First Additional Sessions Judge, Sujit Kumar, on 30 October rejected the Banbhoolpura police's application to stay a Haldwani magistrate's order of 6 October to register an FIR over Form 7s seeking the deletion of 28 electors (form7-36), Dainik Jagran and Live Hindustan reported on 11 November. It also reports the complainant's account that he went to Delhi on 30 October and raised the case with more than 20 MPs and senior leaders of the INDIA bloc, among them Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi, P. Chidambaram, Mahua Moitra and Mehbooba Mufti.
